subject: [PATCH v5 0/3] mm: zswap: free cold writeback folios promptly

reviews.author: Barry Song
reviews.summary: Reviewer Barry Song expressed concern about the need for a sleepable context after Wenjian's commit, questioning its necessity given that folio_unmap_invalidate() is no longer called for unmapped folios.
reviews.raw_body:
Thanks very much, Alexandre. I find the code is really much,
much better, but I’m still struggling to understand why we need a
sleepable context after Wenjian’s commit:

https://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/akpm/mm.git/commit/?id=848d2ce2fce15fbdc083fbf9691bfa72911033c4

With this question:

https://lore.kernel.org/linux-mm/CAGsJ_4wj6XvPB+QF+_X1BJ_8Y2sZEEFAw6RaJJz-cHaDWLkxaQ@mail.gmail.com/T/#u

In short, it still feels a little strange to me that we need a
sleepable context, especially now that we no longer call
`folio_unmap_invalidate()` for unmapped folios.

Best Regards
Barry

reviews.author: Alexandre Ghiti
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Alexandre Ghiti noted that the patch does not handle the case where a swap cache folio is already on the LRU, and requested that the code be modified to check for this condition before dropping the folio from the LRU.

Reviewer Alexandre Ghiti noted that zswap writeback folios are not on LRU due to the percpu LRU cache holding a reference, preventing remove_mapping() from freeing the folio; he suggested using folio_lock() instead of folio_trylock() because it can sleep and requires a sleepable context.
reviews.raw_body:
Hi Barry,

On Mon, Sep 14, 2026 at 1:01 AM Barry Song <baohua@kernel.org> wrote:

---

The thing is the zswap writeback folios are not on lru: that's because
if we put them on lru at allocation, the perpcu lru cache holds a
reference and it prevents remove_mapping() from freeing the folio (I
measured that with on-lru folios, the freed rate collapses from 99.9%
to ~3%).

So if we use the folio_trylock() approach, we'd need to put the folio
back on lru otherwise it would be "lost". But I don't think we can do
that while someone else holds the folio lock.

That's why I use folio_lock() which can sleep and then needs the
sleepable context.

What do you think?

Thanks,

Alex

2026-09-14.patch_summary: This patch set extends the existing dropbehind mechanism to swap cache folios and allows zswap to opt into it, reducing memory residency by freeing cold writeback folios promptly instead of leaving them for page reclaim.
